question.problem:
$$ A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]. $$ Given the matrices above, write the following expression as a Hadamard product. Here $(\,\cdot \,)$ denotes matrix multiplication.
$(AB)\cdot (By)=\,\,$ $3$ $⊙$ {{field-1}}
{{field-2}} {{field-3}}
question.worked_solution:
The Hadamard product of two compatible vectors $u$ and $v$ can be expressed as the matrix product

$$
v⊙u=\text{diag}(v)u.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
AB=[\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
By=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence, 

$$
\begin{aligned}(AB)\cdot (By) & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\text{diag}([\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}])[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]⊙[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
